title: Running a dry cleaning business while keeping the studio
summary: After Dover failed he ran a large dry cleaning and laundry operation to pay bills, while paying others to run the studio; the interviewer met him then.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Well, you're getting ahead. You're kind of getting ahead of me. I was... Yeah, I know. I know.
But that's okay. But the thought struck me.

I know. I know. I know. I know. But I can imagine. But that kind of, now that we're on it, I mean, that kind of blew your... Took the wind out of your sails, and you probably almost wanted to give up on the record business. I'll tell you.
Well, I was forced to. I had to run another business for a couple of years, you know, to make money. So I ran a large dry cleaning and laundry operation.

That's when I first met you. And I couldn't believe it. I was like 72, 73. Somewhere in there, yeah. Yeah. And I was called, I think called Mary Ledbetter. And she said, oh, we have to call Cos over this dry cleaning.

And I couldn't, I couldn't, because I couldn't fathom, well, what is Cosmo doing working for dry cleaners? I was... Yeah, well, I was actually running it. Running, running, running a dry cleaning place. Well... At that time. You know, you pay your rent. You buy your groceries.
You know, you put clothes on your kids.

And so that's what I was doing. But I still was maintaining the studio. You know, I got together a little junk equipment. And I had people over there running it.
